thread:
maya: Quick sanity-check thread for DOVE embeddings (tiling + sparsity-aware quant). I ran the initial onboard sweep against news-100k holdout and seeing weird cluster fragmentation. posting results + logs

jon: Ok drop the numbers?

maya: Baseline (FP16) recall@1=0.732, recall@5=0.911, silhouette=0.42. DOVE int6-perchannel (sparsity-aware quant) recall@1=0.683, recall@5=0.889, silhouette=0.31. Big drop at R@1 and silhouette.

priya: That R@1 delta (~0.049) is larger than we'd expect. Is this the tiling preproc difference or quantization?

maya: I toggled tiling off -> int6 w/o tiling gives R@1=0.700, silhouette=0.35. So tiling amplifies degradation. Seems like dense->sparse tiling boundary introduces embedding shift.

luis: Do we have distribution shift plots? UMAP or PCA?

maya: Pasting quick UMAP observation: many clusters look elongated and form parallel bands for long documents (tiling overlap). Short docs cluster ok. Also seeing higher L2 norms variance (sigma went from 0.12 -> 0.23).

jon: Can you paste the exact commands / config used?

maya: Command used: `python eval_onboard.py --model dovex-small --quant=int6_perchannel --tiling=overlap-25 --holdout news-100k --metrics recall@1,5,silhouette`

priya: Thanks. Two hypotheses: quantization noise interacts with tiling aggregation (avg pool vs CLS) causing vector bias; or pruning/ sparsity budget in quant step is dropping important dims.

luis: What pooling are we using?

maya: Current pipeline: per-tile CLS token, then mean-aggregate across tiles (no norm correction). Try switching to L2-normalize each tile before mean.

jon: Also try per-channel dequant scale calibration on a small calibration set (10k). We saw per-channel reduce bias for other models.

maya: Will run both. quick diff log: `R@1: int6_perchannel (tiling, no tile-norm) = 0.683` -> `int6_perchannel (tiling, tile-L2-norm) = 0.705` (after one pass). silhouette improved 0.31 -> 0.36.

priya: Nice, so normalization recovers ~half the gap. Next try: quantize with smaller sparsity prune (sparsity=0.2 -> 0.05) and rerun.

ci-bot: CI:eval-run 1789012345 started by maya. Status -> queued

maya: Also saw failure mode on KNN: more ID flips at k=1 (flip rate +2.6%). Suggest capturing a few examples where FP16 neighbor != int6 neighbor and inspecting token-level activations.

jon: Can you dump nearest neighbor examples to gist? put one example with long doc tiling overlap, one short.

maya: Will do. early prioritization: 1) Run per-tile L2 norm + re-eval (maya) 2) Per-channel calibration with 10k calibrate set (jon) 3) Sparsity budget sweep 0.0/0.05/0.1/0.2 (priya) 4) Collect 50 NN diff examples and annotate (luis).

priya: ETA for runs? I can start the sparsity sweep on staging GPUs later today.

maya: Good. If anyone sees larger regressions on other holds (QA or reviews) ping here. I'll attach gist logs when available. :mag_right: 

luis: If normalization + calibration fixes >80% of gap we can consider making tile-norm a default transform for DOVE onboard.

jon: Also flag for ops: we should avoid auto-rollout to dedicated until we verify these config choices.

ci-bot: CI:eval-run 1789012345 status -> running on runner-12

maya: thanks all — I'll post results in this thread and add a small notebook with comparison plots.

priya: :thumbsup:
